Lemonbeam's own pipeline (not raw-dump), with MVP_MODEL temporarily swapped from openai/gpt-5 to openai/gpt-5.6-luna for this model-comparison test -- not yet a permanent decision, see test-runs/README.md and DECISIONS.md for the standing model choice. This is the key proof point for the fixed-budget architecture: moment's real content (2,543,012 tokens) exceeds gpt-5.6-luna's own 1,050,000-token window, so a raw-dump-to-model approach could not process this repo at all regardless of which model is used. Lemonbeam processed it in 27.73s for $0.0176 by sending only its evidence-selected 58,279 prompt tokens, same mechanism as every other repo -- the pipeline doesn't care about total repo size, only about what its scoring rubric selects.

prompt tokens (58,279) are noticeably higher than express's equivalent run (35,676) -- expected, since moment has a much larger and more complex codebase producing more chunks that legitimately score above zero for each section, filling more of the ~60-63K total budget.

New failure mode observed here that hadn't shown up on express: several files (moment.js, min/moment.min.js, min/locales.js, min/moment-with-locales.js, min/moment-with-locales.min.js, min/locales.min.js, src/test/moment/create.js, src/test/moment/duration.js, src/test/moment/locale.js) are reported as 'could not be analyzed -- Invalid argument' rather than budget-excluded. This is a distinct, unexamined issue -- a parsing/chunking failure, not a scoring or budget one -- worth investigating separately. All of the min/*.js files are generated/minified build artifacts, so their failure is likely low-stakes (arguably shouldn't be chunked as source at all), but moment.js (the built root-level artifact) and the three src/test/moment/*.js failures are less obviously safe to ignore and weren't diagnosed as part of this test.

Citations were not independently hand-verified for this run the way they were for express -- worth a quick spot-check before treating this result as fully validated.

## Project Overview

Moment.js is a JavaScript date and time library for parsing, validating, manipulating, and formatting dates [README.md:1-20]. The repository is the maintained Moment.js 2.x codebase, described as a dependency-free date and time API with a large locale catalog and compatibility-focused legacy support [AGENTS.md:3-14]. It is in maintenance mode and does not accept new features [README.md:1-20][CONTRIBUTING.md:8-23].

The main technologies visible in the repository are JavaScript, Rollup-based bundling, pnpm scripts, QUnit tests, ESLint, Prettier, Markdownlint, and TypeScript declaration testing [package.json][eslint.config.js][scripts/test.js:44-120]. The project also maintains handwritten TypeScript declarations, including separate declarations for older TypeScript consumers and the `ts3.1-typings` directory [AGENTS.md:36-44][moment.d.ts:22-22][ts3.1-typings/moment.d.ts:34-48].

The primary source entry point appears to be `src/moment.js`, which the build and test scripts bundle into CommonJS, UMD, and ESM outputs [scripts/build.js:213-238][scripts/test.js:44-68]. Locale modules under `src/locale` are built separately and bundled alongside Moment when required [scripts/build.js:133-149][scripts/build.js:163-187]. The published package is named `moment` and is version `2.31.0` in the supplied metadata [package.json].

## Setup / Installation

Development requires Git and Node.js [CONTRIBUTING.md:60-77]. The repository's contributor instructions install pnpm version `11.22.0` globally with `npm install --global pnpm@11.22.0` [CONTRIBUTING.md:60-77]. The repository's agent instructions also state that development tooling uses the Node and pnpm versions declared in `package.json`, although the supplied `package.json` evidence does not show a pnpm version declaration [AGENTS.md:3-14][package.json].

Clone the repository, enter its directory, install pnpm, install dependencies, and switch to the `develop` branch with the documented commands [CONTRIBUTING.md:60-77]:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/moment/moment.git
cd moment
npm install --global pnpm@11.22.0
pnpm install
git checkout develop
```

The repository excludes `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, and `bun.lock`, while its contributor instructions use pnpm, so pnpm is the documented development package manager [CONTRIBUTING.md:60-77][.gitignore]. The development dependencies include Rollup, QUnit, TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, Markdownlint, `npm-run-all2`, `nyc`, and `uglify-js` [package.json].

The repository has no runtime dependencies according to the agent instructions [AGENTS.md:45-62]. The supplied setup documentation does not define required application environment variables, so no environment-variable configuration is documented in the available evidence [CONTRIBUTING.md:60-77][AGENTS.md:3-14].

## Running Locally

The repository does not show a browser application or a local development server command. Its documented local workflow is command-line based and centers on validation, tests, linting, and artifact builds [CONTRIBUTING.md:60-77][CONTRIBUTING.md:106-129].

Run the complete validation workflow with:

```bash
pnpm validate
```

This command runs tests and lint checks [CONTRIBUTING.md:60-77]. The `validate` script itself is not included in the supplied `package.json` excerpt, but the contributor documentation identifies it as a supported command [CONTRIBUTING.md:106-129].

Run the test suite, watch tests, generate coverage, lint, format, or build development artifacts with the following commands [CONTRIBUTING.md:106-129]:

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm test:watch
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm format
pnpm build
```

The visible package scripts map `test` to `node scripts/test.js`, `build` to `node scripts/build.js`, `lint` to ESLint, Markdownlint, a month-parsing check, and Prettier verification, and `format` to Prettier [package.json]. The build produces development artifacts under `build/`, including UMD and ESM Moment bundles, locale bundles, and combined locale bundles [scripts/build.js:213-277].

A focused test can be selected with the `--only` option passed through pnpm, such as `pnpm test -- --only=locale/<locale>` for a locale test [AGENTS.md:36-44][.agents/skills/locale-review/SKILL.md:288-327]. The test runner accepts `moment`, `locale`, or individual test paths as selections [scripts/test.js:15-41].

No local development port is shown in the supplied evidence. The only explicit port is `443`, used by a locale-maintenance script for GitHub's HTTPS API, not for a local application server [scripts/locales.js:75-112].

## Project Structure

Authoritative implementation code is under `src/` [AGENTS.md:15-35]. Core behavior is organized under `src/lib`, including creation and parsing, durations, formatting, Moment instance methods, parsing utilities, date units, and general utilities [src/lib/create/date-from-array.js:1-35][src/lib/duration/add-subtract.js:3-21][src/lib/format/format.js:17-107][src/lib/moment/compare.js:5-72][src/lib/parse/token.js:7-36][src/lib/units/month.js:24-35][src/lib/utils/extend.js:3-19].

Locale definitions live in `src/locale`, and locale tests live in `src/test/locale` [AGENTS.md:15-35][CONTRIBUTING.md:78-105]. The build script discovers locale source files from `src/locale` and emits generated locale bundles under `build/umd` [scripts/build.js:213-231][scripts/build.js:133-149].

Tests are divided into core Moment tests under `src/test/moment` and locale tests under `src/test/locale` [AGENTS.md:15-35]. Shared test helpers are under `src/test/helpers`, including locale helpers, deprecation handling, iteration utilities, DST utilities, and property helpers [src/test/helpers/common-locale.js:57-67][src/test/helpers/deprecation-handler.js:46-62][src/test/helpers/dst.js:3-8][src/test/helpers/each.js:1-6].

Build, test, release, locale, and package-validation tooling is under `scripts/` [scripts/build.js:11-28][scripts/test.js:9-21][scripts/locales.js:9-19]. Benchmark definitions are under `benchmarks/`, and `scripts/benchmark.js` loads and executes them [scripts/benchmark.js:14-36][CONTRIBUTING.md:106-129].

Type declaration sources are at `moment.d.ts` and under `ts3.1-typings`, while TypeScript test configurations are under `typing-tests/legacy` and `typing-tests/modern` [AGENTS.md:36-44][moment.d.ts:327-356][ts3.1-typings/moment.d.ts:370-428][typing-tests/legacy/tsconfig.json][typing-tests/modern/tsconfig.json]. The `meteor` directory contains a separate package description for using Moment with Meteor.js [meteor/README.md:1-7].

The root `moment.js`, `locale/`, `dist/`, and `min/` directories are generated release artifacts and should not be edited manually during ordinary development [AGENTS.md:15-35][CONTRIBUTING.md:24-37].

## Testing

The test framework is QUnit, invoked by `scripts/test.js` through the QUnit command-line runner and a custom reporter [scripts/test.js:83-120][scripts/qunit-reporter.js:2-31]. The QUnit dependency is listed among the development dependencies [package.json].

Run all tests with:

```bash
pnpm test
```

The test script discovers JavaScript files in `src/test/moment` and `src/test/locale` unless a focused `--only` selection is provided [scripts/test.js:15-41]. Before executing QUnit, it bundles the Moment source, all locale modules, and the selected test files with Rollup [scripts/test.js:44-116].

Run a focused locale test with:

```bash
pnpm test -- --only=locale/<locale>
```

This focused command is the documented workflow for locale development and review [AGENTS.md:36-44][.agents/skills/locale-review/SKILL.md:288-327]. The repository requires locale changes to include corresponding unit tests [CONTRIBUTING.md:24-37][CONTRIBUTING.md:78-105].

The repository also provides these testing commands [CONTRIBUTING.md:106-129]:

```bash
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm test:typescript
pnpm validate
```

`pnpm test:coverage` runs the test suite through `nyc` and generates an LCOV report [package.json][CONTRIBUTING.md:106-129]. `pnpm test:typescript` runs declaration tests across multiple TypeScript versions, including legacy and modern configurations [package.json][CONTRIBUTING.md:106-129]. The supplied scripts show TypeScript test projects under `typing-tests/legacy` and `typing-tests/modern` [typing-tests/legacy/tsconfig.json][typing-tests/modern/tsconfig.json].

Tests use QUnit-style `test` blocks and assertions such as `assert.equal`, `assert.ok`, and `assert.deepEqual` [src/test/moment/calendar.js:8-19][src/test/moment/is_valid.js:7-17][src/test/moment/to_type.js:6-22]. Tests also cover expected deprecation warnings through `test.expectedDeprecations` [src/test/moment/add_subtract.js:108-108][src/test/moment/getters_setters.js:46-50]. Shared helpers support locale checks, deprecation handling, iteration, DST-sensitive tests, and object-property checks [src/test/helpers/common-locale.js:57-67][src/test/helpers/deprecation-handler.js:46-62][src/test/helpers/dst.js:3-8].
